newsitem.title: USA: Yellow offers early retirment, sees layoffs. [CORRECTED 01:10 GMT 05/12]
newsitem.headline: Yellow offers early retirment, sees layoffs. [CORRECTED 01:10 GMT 05/12]

text.p: Yellow Corp said Wednesday it has offered early retirment packages to 153 employees and expects to announce layoffs as part of a restructuring of its Yellow Freight System unit.

The company also said it will take an unspecified charge in the fourth quarter for the costs of certain early retirement program, employee severance and other reorganization expenses. (Company corrects from "costs of the early retirement..." to "costs of certain early retirement...")
A Yellow spokesman said the decision on how many layoffs there would be will be made within 30 days and estimated that one to two percent of the company's 24,700 employees would likely be laid off.
The number of layoffs will be determined, in part, by the number of employees who opt for early retirement, Yellow said.
Yellow also said it was creating five individual business units organized by geographic region for its Yellow Freight business.
Each geographic unit will have a group vice president that reports to Yellow Freight president Bill Zollars, while five officers at the central office will also report to Zollars, the company said.
"We are decentralizing responsibility for the business processes that touch the customer in an effort to be more responsive to their ... needs," Zollars said.

"All members of the leadership and management teams will be focused and incentive-based on four priorities," said Zollars. "Those areas are customer satisfaction, improved profitability, revenue growth and operating safely."
Early retirement was offered to 153 employees who are 55 or older and have at least 20 years of service, Yellow said. Those employees have until January 15, 1997 to make their decisions.
